text: Kashmere Gate to Nehru Place. The timetable says forty-eight minutes, at any hour of the day. But leave at six in the evening, and you'll sit on that bus for seventy-nine.
Because traffic isn't one number. The same ride takes thirty-one minutes at dawn, and almost eighty at rush hour.
The buses already know this. So we asked them. A full month of Delhi bus GPS: four hundred million positions, from six thousand buses.
We snapped every point onto its route, threw out the bad ones, and timed every bus between every pair of stops. Thirty-nine million timings.
From those, the model learns four things: the distance, the hour, the road itself, and that road's own rush hour.
Then we tested it on a week it had never seen. Forty percent less error than the timetable, at every single hour.

And it isn't just a chart. It's a planner. Six p.m., Kashmere Gate to Nehru Place: seventy-nine minutes on the bus. Tap five a.m., and it drops to thirty-two. Every road shows its speed. Live buses move on the map. And every stop shows what's coming next.
Delhi bus times. Real buses, real times. Run it on your own laptop.
